land.text: the Kingdom of Hadramawt around Shabwa and the Wadi Hadramawt, with the former Qataban lands

successors.note: Hadhramaut page: it 'ceased to exist by the end of the 3rd century CE, having been annexed by the Himyarite Kingdom'. Himyar page: 'Haḍramaut c. 300 CE'; History of Yemen page: Shammar Yahri'sh conquered Hadramout in 275. Cliopatria's Hadhramaut row runs to 305 and its Himyarite shape widens to 296k km2 (to 52.4 E) in 306.

capitals.name: Shabwa
capitals.note: 'Its capital was Shabwa, not far from the city of Teman' (Teman was Qataban's capital); the page gives no capital years. The Shabwa page: 'first settled in 13th century BC, and ... destroyed by the Himyarites at the end of the 3rd century AD'. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Shabwa.

keyframe_review.note: 85,919 km2 (46.1-52.0 E, 14.7-16.7 N), -700..-351. The Hadhramaut page gives no area and no extent for the kingdom: it says the region 'spanned from modern-day Aden in the west across Dhofar to the east' and 'always included the Wadi Hadhramaut' and the Empty Quarter to its north, which describes the region, not the kingdom. The capital Shabwa (47.0 E) lies inside the shape. The kingdom is first attested c. 700-680 in Karib'il Watar's Sirwah inscription. Extent unverified; the shape stays Cliopatria's. The Awsan share of the late 7th century (ledger) falls inside or beside it.

86,171 km2, -350..183, the previous shape (+0.3 percent). 'Hadhramaut became independent from Sheba in c. 330 BCE' and allied with the Minaeans and Qataban; the History of Yemen page: 'By the 3rd century BC, Qataban, Hadramout and Ma'in became independent from Saba'. The shape does not change; the vassal_end is in this ledger (-330) and in sabaeans. Cliopatria's Qataban row begins in -350.

97,893 km2 (44.3-52.0 E), 184..282: the shape reaches west to 44.29 E, Qataban's western edge, when Cliopatria's Qataban row ends in 183. The Qataban page: 'Ḥaḍramawt and Ḥimyar divided its territories among themselves and annexed them in the late 1st century CE'; the Himyar page has Qataban vanquished 'c. 200 CE' and, in its body, conquered by Hadramawt. The pages disagree with each other and with the shape by one to two centuries; the shape stands for the Qataban land. No infobox area.
98,062 km2, 283..298: +0.2 percent over the previous shape; no page explains it. Neighbour: Cliopatria's Himyarite shape (136,986 km2) from 283.

correction.text: Unchanged shape, held to 300 instead of 305

keyframe_review.note: 98,062 km2, 299..305, unchanged. The Himyar page: 'Qataban in c. 200 CE, and Haḍramaut c. 300 CE'; the Hadhramaut page: it 'ceased to exist by the end of the 3rd century CE'; the Shabwa page: destroyed by the Himyarites at the end of the 3rd century AD; History of Yemen: 275. Years only: 299..300.

region.text: the Hadramawt kingdom around Shabwa and the Wadi Hadramawt

ledger.note: c. 700: Hadramawt at Shabwa. 'The Kingdom of Hadhramaut was established in the early 1st millennium BCE'; 'Hadhramaut and its god Sin are mentioned in the inscription of Surwah by the Makrib Sabean writer Karib'il Watar I around 700-680 BCE' (page). -700 is Cliopatria's first shape and the start of the first dated mention.

region.text: the Hadhramaut kingdom, conquered by Karib'il Watar

ledger.note: c. 675 (bridged): Hadhramaut falls under Saba. The Sabaeans page (reopened 2026-10-19): 'Karib'il conquered all surrounding neighbours, including the Awsan, Qataban, and Hadhramaut' (reign 'late 8th and early 7th centuries BCE'; the Hadhramaut page has Hadhramaut named in Karib'il's Surwah inscription 'around 700–680 BCE'). The year is placed with the Jawf campaigns, as in sabaeans /ledger/3. Against it, the Awsan page calls Hadhramaut one of Saba's 'other allies at the time' of Awsan's fall, the Sabaeans page says only that after the 6th century BCE Saba 'was unable to maintain its supremacy' against 'Qataban and Hadhramaut', and the Hadhramaut page describes no subjection before its 'independent from Sheba in c. 330 BCE'; so the relation rests on one sentence and is confidence 1. Hadhramaut is the vassal and sabaeans the suzerain; mirrors sabaeans /ledger/3 (reviewer fix: the two ledgers agree).

region.text: Hadhramaut's part of the Awsan land, divided with Qataban

ledger.note: late 7th century: a share of Awsan. 'There is also evidence that Saba, after defeating Awsan, divided the territory between two of its other allies at the time: Qataban and Hadhramaut.' The Awsan page dates the fall to the late 7th century BC and gives no shares. The shape of -700 may already include part of it.

region.text: the Hadhramaut kingdom, independent of Sheba

ledger.note: c. 330: Hadhramaut becomes independent of Saba. 'Hadhramaut became independent from Sheba in c. 330 BCE', then 'allied with the Minaeans and the Kingdom of Qataban' (Hadhramaut page, reopened 2026-10-19); the History of Yemen page: 'By the 3rd century BC, Qataban, Hadramout and Ma'in became independent from Saba'. Mirrors sabaeans /ledger/10 (reviewer fix).

region.text: Qataban's territory, divided between Hadramawt and Himyar

ledger.note: 184 (shape's year): the Qataban lands. 'Ḥaḍramawt and Ḥimyar divided its territories among themselves and annexed them in the late 1st century CE' (Qataban page, whose infobox ends Qataban in the 'Late 1st or late 2nd century CE'); the Himyar page says 'Qataban in c. 200 CE'. 184 is Cliopatria's: Qataban's last shape ends in 183 and Hadhramaut's reaches its western edge. The Himyarite share is in the me-06 dossier. The Shabwa page (reopened 2026-10-19) does not mention Qataban or its annexation.

c. 300: Himyar annexes Hadramawt. 'Qataban in c. 200 CE, and Haḍramaut c. 300 CE' and 'By 300, the Himyarite Kingdom had vanquished other political units (including the Saba, Qataban, and Hadrawat kingdoms)' (Himyar page). The History of Yemen page has Shammar Yahri'sh conquer Hadramout, Najran and Tihama in 275; the Shabwa page puts the destruction of the capital at the end of the 3rd century.
c. 300: Hadramawt ends. The Kingdom of Hadhramaut 'ceased to exist by the end of the 3rd century CE, having been annexed by the Himyarite Kingdom'. Cliopatria's row runs to 305.

wars.name: Qatabanian-Hadramawt coalition against Saba
wars.outcome: No result recorded: the Qataban page says only that at one point in the 1st century BCE Qataban formed a coalition with Hadramawt, Radman and Madhay against the Sabaeans, without details.
wars.note: Years span the century because the page dates it no closer. Zones stay empty on purpose: the Qataban page (reopened 2026-10-19) gives only 'At one point in the 1st century BCE' and states no place of fighting, no outcome and no change of ground.

wars.name: Himyarite conquest of Hadramawt
wars.outcome: Himyar annexed Hadramawt, destroying Shabwa, and ended the kingdom by 300; relations had been 'tense, with both sides waging wars against each other for control of the trade routes and territory in the region'.
wars.note: 275 is History of Yemen's date for Shammar Yahri'sh's conquest of Hadramout; the Himyar page says c. 300. The Hadhramaut page dates none of the earlier Himyarite wars.

certainty.note: No page gives a Hadramawt border; the shape is Cliopatria's and the region the page describes (Aden to Dhofar) is wider than the kingdom.

sources.title: Hadhramaut
sources.note: State article: Shabwa, early 1st millennium, first attestation c. 700-680, independent from Saba c. 330, end by the 3rd century; no area. Reopened 2026-10-19: 'independent from Sheba in c. 330 BCE', no earlier subjection described.

sources.title: Awsan
sources.note: Awsan's fall in the late 7th century and the division of its land between Qataban and Hadhramaut.

sources.title: Qataban
sources.note: Coalition against Saba in the 1st century BCE; Hadramawt and Himyar divide Qataban in the late 1st century CE. Reopened 2026-10-19: the coalition has no place, outcome or ground changed; annexation 'late 1st century CE'.

sources.title: Himyarite Kingdom
sources.note: Himyar conquers Hadramawt c. 300 CE; Qataban c. 200; tense relations.

sources.title: History of Yemen
sources.note: Independence of Hadramout by the 3rd century BC; Shammar Yahri'sh conquers Hadramout in 275.

sources.title: Shabwa
sources.note: Capital: first settled in the 13th century BC, destroyed by the Himyarites at the end of the 3rd century AD. Reopened 2026-10-19: silent on Qataban.

sources.title: Sabaeans
sources.note: Reopened for the vassal pair: 'Karib'il conquered all surrounding neighbours, including the Awsan, Qataban, and Hadhramaut'; reign late 8th and early 7th centuries BCE; after the 6th century Saba 'unable to maintain its supremacy'. Hadhramaut never called subject, vassal or ally.

notes:
Page budget up to 5 pages; six were opened (Hadhramaut, Awsan, Qataban, Himyarite Kingdom, History of Yemen, Shabwa); four of them were also opened for the sabaeans dossier. The Shammar Yuhar'ish article would not load under three URL spellings (listed in the Sabaean notes and the report). No page gives an area, so Cliopatria's 85,919-98,062 km2 are unchecked.

Split decision: the Cliopatria row Hadhramaut -700..305 is one state, the Kingdom of Hadramawt, and is kept as one dossier; the pages give no dynastic or state break.

Open points for a gap-filler: (1) End: c. 300 (Himyar lead), 'in the 4th century' (Himyar body), 'by the end of the 3rd century' (Hadhramaut), end of the 3rd century for Shabwa (Shabwa page) and 275 (History of Yemen); the dossier ends 300, Cliopatria 305. (2) The relation with Saba: the Sabaeans page has Karib'il Watar conquer Hadhramaut, the Awsan page has it Saba's ally, the Sabaeans page says Saba lost supremacy after the 6th century, and the Hadhramaut page has it independent only c. 330. After the review this ledger carries the same vassal pair as sabaeans (vassal_start -675, confidence 1; vassal_end -330, confidence 2), so the two agree; the start rests on one sentence and a gap-filler should read the Seshat or Karib'il Watar page before the tint is drawn. (3) The Qataban absorption at 184 (shape; the Shabwa page, reopened, is silent on it) conflicts with the Qataban page (late 1st century CE) and the Himyar page (c. 200; and, in its body, Hadramawt conquering Qataban before being itself conquered by Himyar 'in the 4th century'). (4) The Hadhramaut page says the kingdom's trade route ran Dhofar-Mahra-Hadramawt-Shabwa and that its borders 'always included the Wadi Hadhramaut' and the Empty Quarter; Dhofar/Mahra are not in Cliopatria's shape and no page dates any Hadramawt rule there. (5) The Aelius Gallus page (opened for the sabaeans dossier) names Hadhramaut, controlled by Ilasaros, among the kingdoms on the Roman march; it supports Hadramawt's independence c. 25 BC but gives no territory. (6) No ruler strip: no list was on the pages. Counterparts without a dossier: Awsan (see sabaeans notes).

Review repair (2026-10-19): added vassal_start -675 / vassal_end -330 (counterpart sabaeans); the Sabaeans page was reopened (outside the 5-page budget). /wars/0 zones are empty because the Qataban page names no place or outcome.
